title: Where does 'however / even so / though' go?
subtitle: Boundaries · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Boundaries are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 14 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Every choice has the same transition word, such as however, therefore, even so, or a trailing though.
- The choices differ only in whether the semicolon, period, or comma sits before or after that word.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the point where one complete sentence ends and the next begins.
- 2) Put the strong break there (a period or semicolon), and put the transition, followed by a comma, at the start of the new clause.
- 3) If the transition only interrupts one clause, and the other side is a phrase rather than a full sentence, set it off with commas on both sides.
- Use a colon after it if what follows explains the clause.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The test is betting that you treat 'however' like 'but' and join two sentences with just a comma.
It is also betting that you'll attach the transition to the wrong clause, by putting the semicolon after the word instead of before it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
